key_insight: Low-frequency bow-shock unsteadiness is governed by a spanwise mass-balance mismatch in the separated flow, with shock-foot motion starting near mid-span and propagating with delay across the span.
engineering_relevance: For supersonic protuberance-induced shock–boundary-layer interactions, the separation length and spanwise reverse-flow structure are key design factors for predicting and controlling shock oscillations.
method: Wind-tunnel experiments at Mach 2.87 with protuberances of varying shapes and sizes
Time-resolved surface pressure measurements and schlieren imaging to characterize shock/separation unsteadiness
Compressible adaptive detached eddy simulation and POD-based modal analysis for a 15 mm cubical protuberance
evidence_signal: The study reports low-frequency shock oscillations at Stδ ~ 0.01, mid-frequency pressure oscillations in the separated region at Stδ ~ 0.1, and confirms the mechanism using 3-D reconstructed modes and two-point correlations.
watch_item: The inferred mechanism is demonstrated in detail for one cubical protuberance case, so generalization to other geometries and flow conditions should be done cautiously.
paper_title: On the governing mechanism of unsteadiness in bow shock-induced three-dimensional separation
